content:
Every proportion question asks one silent question first: when x grows, does y grow with it or shrink? Answer that in the first ten seconds — direct or inverse — and the arithmetic that follows is Class 5 level. Start by testing the ground. The free IMO Class 8 Proportions online test below asks 10 exam-pattern MCQs and scores them on the spot. Each explanation shows the intended one-minute route.

What the IMO asks from Proportions in Class 8

  • Spotting direct vs inverse proportion from a table or story.
  • Direct proportion: x/y constant — maps, recipes, cost, shadows.
  • Inverse proportion: xy constant — workers and days, speed and time, pipes.
  • Two-step problems mixing both types.
  • Finding the constant and predicting a missing value.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Direct: the RATIO x/y stays fixed. Inverse: the PRODUCT xy stays fixed. Test the pair you are given.
  • More taps, less filling time — sharing a fixed job is the classic inverse setup.
  • Map scale problems are direct proportion in disguise: 1 cm : 5 km never changes.
  • If 6 workers need 12 days, the job is 72 worker-days — then ANY crew size divides into it.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Setting up a direct proportion for workers-and-days problems.
  • Inverting the wrong side of the equation when solving for the unknown.
  • Forgetting to convert units before comparing (minutes vs hours ruins the constant).

quiz.title: IMO Class 8 Proportions Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 8: Direct and Inverse Proportions

questions.q: If 12 notebooks cost Rs 540, what is the cost of 18 such notebooks?
questions.explanation: Cost and number of notebooks are in direct proportion. Cost per notebook = 540 / 12 = Rs 45. Cost of 18 notebooks = 45 × 18 = Rs 810.

questions.q: If x varies directly as y and x = 15 when y = 9, find the value of y when x = 35.
questions.explanation: Since x varies directly as y, x/y = constant. k = 15/9 = 5/3. When x = 35: 35/y = 5/3, so y = 35 × 3/5 = 21.

questions.q: If P is directly proportional to Q², and P = 48 when Q = 4, find Q when P = 75.
questions.explanation: P = kQ². Substituting: 48 = k(16), so k = 3. When P = 75: 75 = 3Q², Q² = 25, Q = 5.

questions.q: Two quantities in direct proportion have the ratio 2 : 1. When both are increased by 5, their new ratio becomes 3 : 2. Find the original smaller quantity.
questions.explanation: Let the quantities be 2a and a. After increasing by 5: (2a + 5)/(a + 5) = 3/2. Cross-multiplying: 2(2a + 5) = 3(a + 5), so 4a + 10 = 3a + 15, giving a = 5. The smaller quantity is 5.

questions.q: If x and y are inversely proportional and x = 8 when y = 15, what is the value of xy when x = 12?
questions.explanation: In inverse proportion, the product xy is constant. xy = 8 × 15 = 120. This constant remains 120 regardless of the values of x and y.

questions.q: 15 workers can build a bridge in 20 days. After 4 days of work by all 15, 3 workers leave. How many more days will the remaining 12 workers take to finish?
questions.explanation: Total work = 15 × 20 = 300 worker-days. Work done in 4 days = 15 × 4 = 60. Remaining work = 240 worker-days. With 12 workers: 240/12 = 20 more days.

questions.q: A vehicle travelling at 45 km/h covers a distance in 4 hours 40 minutes. At what speed should it travel to cover the same distance in 3 hours 30 minutes?
questions.explanation: 4 h 40 min = 14/3 hours. Distance = 45 × 14/3 = 210 km. 3 h 30 min = 7/2 hours. Required speed = 210 / (7/2) = 210 × 2/7 = 60 km/h.

questions.q: Three identical pipes can fill a tank in 6 hours. If one pipe is closed, how long will the remaining two pipes take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: 3 pipes fill at rate = 1/6 per hour. Each pipe fills at 1/18 per hour. Two pipes fill at 2/18 = 1/9 per hour. Time = 9 hours.

questions.q: A can do a piece of work in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. How many more days will B take to finish the work alone?
questions.explanation: A's rate = 1/20 per day. B's rate = 1/30 per day. Together = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12 per day. Work done in 4 days = 4/12 = 1/3. Remaining = 2/3. Time for B alone = (2/3) / (1/30) = 20 days.

questions.q: A pasture feeds 24 cows for 40 days or 21 cows for 60 days, with grass growing at a constant rate. How many cows can the pasture feed for 120 days?
questions.explanation: Let initial grass = G, daily growth = g, daily consumption per cow = c. Equations: 24 × 40 x c = G + 40g (so 960c = G + 40g) and 21 × 60 x c = G + 60g (so 1260c = G + 60g). Subtracting: 300c = 20g, so g = 15c. Then G = 9
